event.name: 2026 US midterm election
event.fact: The FEC calendar identifies 3 November 2026 as the federal general-election date. This record does not identify winners or establish a policy change.

nodes.label: Official event record
nodes.summary: The FEC calendar identifies 3 November 2026 as the federal general-election date. This record does not identify winners or establish a policy change.
nodes.question: What actually happened, and when?
nodes.counter: A calendar date does not establish a winner, an enacted policy or a market cause. Even an official policy announcement may have been anticipated.

nodes.label: Policy expectations
nodes.summary: A change in congressional composition could alter expectations for taxation, spending or trade. Enactment, timing and prior pricing matter.
nodes.question: Did expectations change beyond what was already priced?
nodes.counter: No enacted tax, spending or trade change is established by this map. Anticipation, gridlock or unchanged expectations could weaken this link.

nodes.label: Discount rates & credit
nodes.summary: Changes in expected financing costs or discount rates could affect valuations and bond prices, all else equal. The market response need not match the policy-rate change.
nodes.question: Which yields or financing terms actually changed?
nodes.counter: Growth, inflation, term premia and safe-haven demand can move longer yields in another direction. This map has no historical yield-vintage causal model.

nodes.label: Margins & earnings
nodes.summary: Taxes, demand, trade costs and financing conditions could affect expected company cash flows differently across industries.
nodes.question: Is there company-level evidence for the proposed cash-flow channel?
nodes.counter: Pricing power, hedging, foreign revenues and earnings announcements can offset the proposed effect. No company earnings estimate is generated.

nodes.label: Risk appetite & VIX
nodes.summary: Policy uncertainty or its resolution could change demand for risk and options protection. VIX is expected volatility, not a prediction of stock direction.
nodes.question: Does the observed VIX window support or challenge the uncertainty story?
nodes.counter: Inflation releases, earnings, geopolitical events and positioning can also move VIX. A fall in VIX does not identify its cause.

nodes.label: Observed sector windows
nodes.summary: Inspect adjusted ETF returns and SPY differences around the event. These are descriptive observations, not measurements of the arrows above.
nodes.question: What did the available prices actually do?
nodes.counter: Co-occurring returns do not prove causality. Three selected events are insufficient to validate a robust political trading rule. Future sessions remain unavailable.

nodes.label: Your proposed exposure
nodes.summary: Map your entered SPY, GLD, USO and TLT target weights to broad asset exposures; the remainder is cash. No predicted loss or event-specific price sensitivity is calculated.
nodes.question: Which exposures would you investigate before changing your allocation?
nodes.counter: This does not look through ETF holdings, estimate correlations or produce a portfolio forecast. User weights do not alter historical market evidence.

observations.name: US large caps
observations.methodology: Adjusted-price change from the last common trading close before election day. Event session is 0; post-session window ends at +N. Excess return is asset minus SPY, not factor-adjusted alpha. VIX changes are index points, not investable P&L. Coincidence does not establish causation. Macro releases, rates, earnings and positioning are confounders. No election winner, policy change or causal effect is inferred.

notice: A research hypothesis map, not a causal model, forecast or trading recommendation. Official event records, conjectured channels, descriptive price observations and user inputs are different evidence types. Every edge is unestimated. Current news is not used to generate past trading signals. Historical windows use current-vintage adjusted prices; incomplete future windows are labelled partial.
